target_customer: Developers and companies building voice agents and voice products, including enterprises that want on premises models
problem: Text to speech output sounds robotic and flat in conversation. Miso Labs wants voice models with emotion and low latency good enough to pass a voice Turing test.
business_model: Open weight models with a planned paid API and enterprise support and on premises hosting contracts
product_category: Voice AI foundation models (text to speech)

founders.name: Cassidy Dalva
founders.role: Founder/CEO (as listed on the YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists only this founder, with a Stanford alum descriptor. Employers not stated.

founders.name: Aoden Teo
founders.role: CEO and co-founder (per Fondo interview and other profiles)
founders.background_notes: Fondo interview chapter titles describe a path from serious chess player to math obsession. No education or employers found in sources opened. The YC page and the interview disagree on who holds the CEO title.

competitors.name: ElevenLabs
competitors.what: Leading commercial text to speech and voice agent platform
competitors.traction_then: Market leader; Miso claims 700ms latency for it versus 110ms for Miso (vendor claim)

competitors.name: Sesame CSM
competitors.what: Conversational speech model whose design Miso says it draws on

competitors.name: Mistral Voxtral TTS
competitors.what: 4B open weight TTS model reported to rival ElevenLabs on cloning with about 70ms latency

technical_complexity.rationale: Training an 8B parameter emotive speech model with a residual vector quantization transformer and 110ms latency is hard for a team of 2 to 3. The company records its own training data in a studio per the Fondo interview. Training data and pipeline were not released.

defensibility.rationale: Weights are open under a modified MIT license, so the model itself is copyable. Any moat rests on proprietary studio recorded training data and speed of iteration. Well funded rivals ship comparable open models.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to know. Mistral shipped an open TTS model near the same time. No acquisition reported.

market_need_then: Voice agents were a hot category in 2025 and 2026 and builders complained about flat robotic voices and latency. Evidence is mostly company claims and launch coverage in June 2026.

identity.logo: No logo description found in sources
identity.visual_style: Clean minimal layout with a futuristic tone per the company site
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and direct with explicit competitor latency comparisons

branding.brand_signature: The voice Turing test goal and the 110ms latency claim
branding.community_and_virality: Fondo interview reports over 3,000 GitHub stars and 5 million views on X for Miso-1 (company reported). Open weights drew many third party guides.

brand_strength.rationale: Early brand with strong developer attention from an open release, but the name shares its word with Miso Robotics and other companies and no brand assets are documented.

outcome_analysis: Miso Labs is active and very young. It released an open weight 8B emotive text to speech model on 3 June 2026 right after its Spring 2026 batch, which drew strong developer attention. No round could be verified, no exit has occurred, and rivals such as ElevenLabs, Sesame and Mistral compete directly, so the outcome is still open.
notes: Funding unverified: one AI tools directory lists $8M+ seed with Gradient Ventures and General Catalyst, a job board lists $130K total. No press release found, so no round is recorded. Competition list is from June 2026 launch coverage near the batch, and latency figures are vendor claims. YC page and other profiles differ on which founder is CEO.
